verdict.rationale: Crossmint exposes webhooks for wallet and order events (transfers, signer exports, payment status) that could be wired into external automation, and it lets users define scoped spending rules (caps, counterparties, time windows) under which an agent can act automatically without per-action prompts. However, there is no evidence of a native rule engine where a user declares 'on event X, trigger action Y' inside Crossmint itself — automation still requires building your own listener/orchestration on top of the webhooks.  missing for 10: a built-in conditional trigger/rule-definition UI or API (if-this-then-that style), evidence of chained multi-step automated actions, and any first-party example of event-to-action wiring beyond webhook delivery.
